## Body

**Performance: BLOCK P170-F001** at `bfe2301bdbf6cc62d7f720270fabc11a8fcc17df`.

**P170-F001: the new repeated prune launches search PATH.** `pr-freeze.ts:631` passes bare `gh` for every distinct PR; `:636` and `:659` pass bare `git` for every candidate status and removal. The unchanged real runner at `:709-710` directly calls `spawnSync(program, ...)`, without resolving or caching an absolute executable path. The PR activates that runner on new repeated batch paths. No shell is involved, but shell-free spawning does not eliminate PATH lookup.

This violates AGENTS.md's resource rule: launch by absolute path in any repeated path. It also prevents treating logical runner-call counts as the full machine process price; macOS PATH-miss amplification is the reason for the rule. Exact amplification was not measured here. `/usr/sbin/lsof` is already absolute and is not the finding.

**Required repair:** resolve the tooling executables once per script run to absolute paths, then use those for real launches. Keep the C25/no-node_modules contract and explicit missing-tool errors. Add focused execution-seam proof that repeated git/gh launches receive absolute paths and reuse their resolution; the current injected-runner tests record logical program names and do not prove this.

**Other cost claims checked:** no new timer, recurring poll, launch retry or daemon-side loop. The new finite prune sweeps are on demand. With C matching-name candidates, P distinct PR numbers and R actual removal attempts (including refusals), the normal macOS path makes **3 + P + C + R direct runner calls**: worktree list, seat list, lsof, P gh reads, C statuses, R removals. Dry-run has R=0. Zero candidates stops after the one worktree-list call. PR reads are deduplicated by Set/Map; there is one seat/cwd snapshot, not one per candidate. Wrong-branch/wrong-SHA candidates still pay their gh/status/busy checks before `decide` spares them.

Lsof is one whole-machine process-cwd enumeration, not a per-candidate launch; its stdout is then retained and parsed. Linux instead enumerates `/proc` and reads one cwd link per PID in-process. Candidate matching scans seat and process arrays, O(C*(S+M)) in the worst case; seat-folder realpath calls occur inside that candidate scan and can repeat O(C*S). Command output has a 64 MiB maxBuffer setting, not a whole-job memory bound. No child timeout is configured, so a hung lsof/gh/git can stall this standalone command indefinitely without a retry loop. The supplied author dry-run was about 10 seconds for 13 candidates; it does not isolate lsof's share.

**Daemon boundary:** the script does contact the daemon once through `pij-rs --json list`. It issues no daemon start/stop/restart/control, registration, send or mutation command. Its deliberate mutations are local `git worktree remove` calls, never `--force`; dry-run issues none. The daemon and its launch-site inventory are unchanged, so no new daemon spawn-site guard entry is required. That distinction does not waive the tooling's repeated-launch path rule.

**F109:** the recipe now runs Node's TypeScript stripping directly, with only builtin imports and no tsx/node_modules dependency. Ordinary freeze logic and command counts are otherwise unchanged; this runner change does not compile the project or add standing work.

**CI:** [42429696026](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42429696026) succeeds at this exact SHA. Node 22 and 24 logs each confirm **28 pr-freeze tests passed**, including the real strip-types symlink invocation, plus typecheck and Biome. Read the prune policy/brake, dry-run/fail-closed and cwd-parser cases; they use injected commands/cwd inputs, not a live macOS cost measurement. Rust lint/test and Delivers `42429695920` also succeed. Green CI does not cover P170-F001.

Worktree and GitHub heads agree; clean, CLEAN/MERGEABLE. No local build, test, dry-run, process-cwd census or prune was executed, and no review worktree or daemon was modified. This is a cost block on the new repeated launches, not a verdict on the separate deletion-safety/security review.
